title: Reentrance and temperature chaos in the $p$-spin Ising spin glass
abstract: Reentrant transitions and temperature chaos are two unusual properties of spin glasses and had long been considered physically unrelated. We recently established a logical relation between these two phenomena [Phys. Rev. E 112, 044140 (2025)]. In the present paper, we provide an explicit example of this logical relation in the fully connected Ising $p$-spin glass with a ferromagnetic bias. By expanding the free energy around the triple point, we show analytically that the ferromagnetic--spin glass boundary is reentrant in the vicinity of the triple point throughout the examined range of finite $p>2$. It then follows from the above logical relation that there exists at least one pair of distinct temperatures in the spin glass phase for which the overlap of spin configurations vanishes. This is a necessary condition for temperature chaos, but it would be quite unusual for the overlap to vanish only for selected temperature pairs but not for others within a single spin glass phase. These results therefore strongly suggest the existence of temperature chaos in the sense that the overlaps of spin configurations vanish for all temperature pairs throughout the spin glass phase. Independent evidence for this behavior is provided by a two-temperature replica calculation.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the $p$-spin Ising spin glass model to establish a link between reentrant phase transitions and temperature chaos. By showing that the phase boundary reenters, the authors deduce that the system must exhibit temperature chaos, meaning the spin-state overlap vanishes for all pairs of temperatures within the spin glass phase. This advances the understanding of complex glassy dynamics in disordered quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the physical relationship between two unusual properties in spin glasses: reentrant phase transitions and temperature chaos.
main_result: The authors analytically demonstrate that the ferromagnetic–spin glass boundary is reentrant for the $p$-spin Ising spin glass, which strongly suggests the existence of temperature chaos across the entire spin glass phase.
method: The analysis involves expanding the free energy around the triple point and utilizing the contrapositive of a proposition relating reentrance to the existence of temperature chaos.
model_or_system: The system studied is the fully connected Ising $p$-spin glass with a ferromagnetic bias, described by a Hamiltonian involving $p$-body interactions. The analysis uses replica calculations and free energy minimization techniques.
key_observables: The primary observables are the curvature of the ferromagnetic–spin glass phase boundary and the two-temperature spin-state overlap distribution, $P_2(x |  eta_1,  eta_2)$.
important_parameters: The key parameters include the spin interaction order $p$ (specifically $p>2$), the inverse temperatures ($ eta_1,  eta_2$), and the system size $N$ (taken to infinity).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that if the overlap vanishes for one temperature pair, it implies the vanishing of overlap for all pairs within the spin glass phase. The analysis also relies on the NOO proposition and the validity of the replica calculations.
figures_summary: The notes reference a schematic phase diagram for $p=3$ showing the PM, 1RSB-SG, RS-FM, and Nishimori Line boundaries, and a table listing calculated values for various parameters across different $p$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by establishing the logical connection between reentrance and temperature chaos, provides an explicit analytical calculation for the $p$-spin model showing reentrance, and supports this conclusion with independent two-temperature replica calculations.
why_interesting: The study of spin glasses and their phase transitions is foundational to understanding complex energy landscapes, which has parallels in optimizing quantum circuits or analyzing complex many-body quantum dynamics.
